recall.minute: Quality attributes, or non-functional requirements, are measurable properties that qualify how well a system performs its functions. They group into operational (availability, performance, scalability, reliability), structural (portability, maintainability, configurability, extensibility) and cross-cutting (security, usability, accessibility, legal) attributes. A sale-day crash versus a smooth 25-million-viewer stream shows that identifying key attributes and choosing a matching architecture (microservices on Kubernetes) is decisive. Requirements must be SMART, for example 99.95% annual uptime. ML adds accuracy, robustness, explainability, fairness, drift adaptability and monitoring, and reproducibility, shaped by problem type, approach, training and data, as the fraud-detection case shows. Quality requirements drive architecture: the structures, elements and relationships of the system, which for ML systems also spans hardware, data, ML and deployment components, as in a RAG chatbot. Architects think beyond the model and reuse patterns, expressed as context, problem and solution, such as pipe-and-filter for ML pipelines.
